IPoliticsBbsVisitorUser.IJoin.description:
Request body for visitor account registration on the politicsBbs discussion board. Creates temporary guest accounts that provide session management for unauthenticated users, enabling tracking of visitor activity and basic personalization features. Visitor accounts receive limited JWT tokens for session continuity while maintaining appropriate security for guest users.

This registration DTO supports the politicsBBS platform's visitor system for temporary access to political and economic discussions. The visitor accounts provide basic session management capabilities while maintaining anonymity and limited privileges appropriate for guest users.

The authentication model supports different user types through a polymorphic ownership pattern where visitors, members, and moderators have distinct access levels and capabilities. Visitor accounts are designed for temporary browsing of economic policy discussions and political analysis content.

The session tracking fields (ip, href, referrer) enable comprehensive audit trails and analytics for visitor behavior analysis while maintaining appropriate privacy boundaries for guest users who browse political discourse content.

Username validation ensures consistent display across article access and comment viewing activity while preventing impersonation or confusion with authenticated member accounts in the discussion forum interface.

href.description: Connection URL (current page URL) - MANDATORY. Provides session context for tracking visitor entry points and navigation patterns. Must be a valid URI format reflecting the actual page from which registration is initiated.

ip.description: Client IP address for session tracking and audit purposes. Optional field that may be provided by the client for SSR scenarios or when server cannot reliably extract IP from request headers while maintaining privacy boundaries for visitor accounts.

password.description: Password for the visitor account. Must meet complexity requirements: minimum 8 characters including at least one uppercase letter, one lowercase letter, and one number. Used for authentication and session management with visitor-level security constraints reflecting temporary account nature.

referrer.description: Referrer URL (previous page URL) - MANDATORY. Tracks how visitors arrive at the site for analytics and session attribution. Must be a valid URI format representing the page that led to registration, can be empty string for direct access.

username.description: Unique username for the visitor account. Must be 3-20 characters using only letters, numbers, and hyphens. Used for display purposes and session identification in visitor contexts while excluding personal identifiers appropriate for guest accounts.

Response body for visitor authorization on the politicsBBS discussion board. Provides comprehensive visitor account details with JWT authentication tokens for session management across the political and economic discourse platform.

This authorization response contains the complete visitor account profile following successful authentication, supporting the polymorphic ownership pattern where visitors receive limited session capabilities appropriate for temporary guest users engaging with policy discussions and economic analysis content.

The response structure enables visitor session management through JWT tokens while maintaining appropriate security boundaries for unauthenticated users browsing political discourse and economic policy debates. Visitor accounts support read-only access to approved articles, comments, and community discussions.

Account details include unique visitor identification with timestamps for activity tracking and session management across the discussion platform. The JWT tokens provide secure authentication for subsequent API interactions while reflecting the temporary nature of guest user access to political and economic content.

The visitor system enables basic platform functionality including article browsing, comment viewing, and search operations while maintaining appropriate security constraints for guest users who engage with political discourse and economic policy analysis through the politics discussion board interface.

username.description: Visitor's username from politics_bbs_visitors.username field used for display and session identification in visitor contexts with URL-safe formatting constraints.

password_hash.description: Secure password hash from politics_bbs_visitors.password_hash field used for authentication verification using bcrypt or similar secure hashing algorithms.

refresh_token.description:
The refresh token used to obtain a new access token. This long-lived token is stored in the session management tables and enables secure token rotation for maintaining session continuity without requiring re-authentication.

The refresh token implements a security-by-design approach to session management, providing:
- Extended session validity without exposing long-term credentials
- Automatic token rotation to maintain security hygiene
- Temporary nature reflecting guest session requirements
- Graceful session expiration handling

This token is particularly crucial for visitor sessions that need temporary guest account functionality while maintaining appropriate security boundaries for unauthenticated users who access the political discussion platform.

IPoliticsBbsUser.IRefresh.description:
Request body for refreshing authentication tokens on the politicsBbs discussion board system. This DTO enables visitor sessions and member accounts to maintain active authentication state by exchanging valid refresh tokens for new access tokens.

The refresh mechanism provides a balance between security and user experience:
- Long-lived refresh tokens stored securely in session tables
- Short-lived access tokens for regular API operations
- Automatic token rotation to prevent session hijacking
- Graceful handling of expired tokens with appropriate error responses

For visitor sessions, this endpoint supports temporary guest accounts that can maintain viewing history and basic platform preferences while preserving the security model appropriate for unauthenticated sessions. Member accounts receive standard JWT management with session management tables tracking their security context.

The refresh process validates existing tokens against database records, ensures token integrity, and generates new tokens with updated expiration times while maintaining the user's authentication context. This design ensures both security and session continuity for iBbs platform users.

through proper format validation and database username uniqueness constraints.

password.description:
Moderator's password for authentication verification.

Must meet security requirements of minimum 8 characters including at least
one uppercase letter, one lowercase letter, and one number. The password is
verified against the securely stored password_hash in the politics_bbs_moderators
table using bcrypt or similar secure hashing algorithms.

oneOf.description: Client IP address for session tracking - optional but recommended

ip.description:
Client IP address for session context and audit logging.

tracking and geographic analysis of administrative access patterns.
When not provided, the server attempts to extract the IP from the connection
metadata, but client provision can improve accuracy, especially in SSR contexts.

href.description:
Connection URL for session audit tracking - required field.

and session context. This field is mandatory to maintain comprehensive logs
of moderator authentication events and support proper security monitoring
of administrative access to the politicsBBS platform.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL for session audit tracking - required field.

for understanding navigation patterns and supporting security analysis.
This required field helps track moderator access sources and maintain
comprehensive audit trails for administrative activity on the politicsBBS
discussion board platform.

IPoliticsBbsCategory.ISummary.description:

This summary type is specifically optimized for combination with article information, navigation interfaces, and category selection components within the politicsBBS discussion platform.

The summary provides essential category information while maintaining performance efficiency through selective field inclusion. All intrinsic identifier fields (id, code, name) and configuration attributes (sequence, primary, required, multiplicative) are included to support all category-related UI operations without requiring additional database queries.

This format balances comprehensive category information resolution needs with network efficiency requirements, enabling the atomic operation principle by providing sufficient context in a single API call. The summary is particularly valuable for member dashboards, article creation flows, and browsing interfaces where category context enhances content understanding while maintaining system performance for substantive political and economic discussions.

IPoliticsBbsCategory.ICreate.description:
Request type for creating a new political discussion category in the politicsBBS system. Categories organize economic and political discussions by topic, facilitating content discovery and filtering within the platform.

Categories serve as the primary organizational structure for the discussion board, enabling users to find relevant content pertaining to economic policies, political analysis, international relations, and other policy-focused topics. The designation helps users navigate discussions by thematic focus rather than chronological order.

The system enforces that articles must belong to at least one category, ensuring all submitted content receives appropriate classification. Categories support both primary featured distinction for prominent display and required/optional settings to enforce organizational consistency throughout the political discourse platform.

code.description: Unique category code for internal reference and URL generation. This code must be globally unique across the system and cannot be changed after creation. Used for URL paths and API references, typically formatted in lowercase with hyphens. Examples: 'economic-policy', 'international-relations', 'domestic-politics'. The code serves as the stable identifier for category references throughout the system.

name.description: Display name for the category shown to users in the interface and navigation. Should be human-readable and clearly describe the category focus while maintaining professional tone appropriate for political and economic discourse. Examples: 'Economic Policy', 'International Relations', 'Domestic Politics'. The name provides the primary visual identifier in user interfaces and search filtering.

description.description: Detailed description of the category's purpose and scope, explaining what types of discussions belong within its domain. Helps users understand content guidelines and supports informed category selection during article creation. Should provide clear guidance about appropriate types of economic analysis, political commentary, or policy discussions that align with the category focus while maintaining substantive discourse standards.

color.description: CSS color code for visual identification and UI theming of the category. Used for visual differentiation in category selectors, article badges, and navigation interfaces to enhance visual recognition. Should be specified as hex color codes like '#1E88E5' for blue themes or '#E53935' for red themes, providing visual consistency across the platform. Can be null to use default system styling.

icon.description: Icon identifier for visual representation in category interfaces and navigation elements. Could be CSS class names (e.g., 'fas fa-economy'), fontawesome identifiers (e.g., 'fa-chart-line'), or other icon references from supported icon libraries. Enhances visual recognition and quick identification in category browsers and selection interfaces. Can be null when visual icons are not required or desired.

sequence.description: Display order for category sorting in lists and selection interfaces. Lower numeric values appear first in category drop-downs, navigation menus, and category selection components. Enables moderator control over presentation hierarchy, allowing popular or important categories to be positioned prominently for improved discoverability of economic and political content.

primary.description: Whether this category should be featured prominently in the interface as a primary discussion area. Primary categories receive enhanced visibility in category selectors, home page displays, and navigation elements to improve discoverability of key economic policy, political analysis, or international relations content areas that represent core discussion focuses of the platform.

required.description: Whether this category is mandatory for articles or optional for content classification. When true, articles must be assigned to this category, ensuring consistent organizational structure for essential taxonomy areas like broad political or economic discussions. Can be used to enforce categorization rules or create mandatory category groups that maintain content organization standards across the political discussion platform.

multiplicative.description: Whether multiple categories can be assigned to content simultaneously. When false, articles can only have this single category identifier. When true, allows flexible categorization where articles can belong to multiple overlapping categories such as both 'Economic Policy' and 'Healthcare Policy' for health economics discussions, supporting nuanced content classification appropriate for complex political and economic topics.

IPoliticsBbsComment.ICreate.description: Request DTO for creating a new comment on a politicsBBS article with support for threaded discussions and user authentication context. This DTO enables members to submit meaningful dialogue while maintaining proper content validation and moderation workflows. The system supports threading with up to 3 levels of nesting depth. When creating a reply to an existing comment, the system calculates the appropriate depth level and validates against the maximum nesting constraint. Comments maintain polymorphic ownership patterns where different user types (visitors, members, moderators) create comments through dedicated subtype relationships based on the authenticated user's role. Content validation ensures comments provide meaningful dialogue while preventing spam and inappropriate content. The operation creates the base comment entity and associated subtype entity based on the user's role type, maintaining proper referential integrity. On successful creation, the system returns the complete comment information including generated IDs and timestamps. Comments are initially created with 'pending' status by default, which moderators can then approve for publication, ensuring quality control over the discussion content while maintaining quick user feedback during the posting process.

Comments should provide substantive discussion content and avoid spam or inappropriate material. Content must remain focused on economic and political topics while maintaining respectful discourse standards.

ip.description: Client IP address for session tracking (OPTIONAL - server can extract, but client may provide for SSR). Used for audit and session management across the discussion platform. Supports both IPv4 and IPv6 formats for comprehensive tracking.

href.description: Connection URL (current page URL) - MANDATORY. Required for proper session context tracking and audit trail. Must be a valid URI pointing to the current discussion page where comment is being submitted.

referrer.description: Referrer URL (previous page URL) - MANDATORY. Required for navigation tracking and user journey analysis. Must be a valid URI pointing to the page that led users to current discussion.

The system implements a polymorphic comment ownership pattern where visitors, members, and moderators create comments through dedicated subtype relationships. Comments support threaded discussions up to 3 levels deep with proper nesting constraint enforcement. Full-text search leverages PostgreSQL's trigram similarity indexing for optimal performance across the politics_bbs_comments table content field.

Filtering capabilities enable content moderation teams to efficiently manage approval workflows, identify potentially problematic discussions, and track community engagement across different user roles. The search functionality helps users discover relevant perspectives on economic policies, political developments, and regulatory discussions while maintaining appropriate privacy boundaries for various participant types.

Pagination support ensures efficient handling of large comment threads while maintaining optimal API performance. IPoliticsBbsSearch.IRequest.description: Request parameters for unified search across all discussion board content including articles, comments, and user-generated content. This search system utilizes PostgreSQL's full-text search capabilities with trigram similarity matching combined with advanced filtering options to provide comprehensive discovery of economic and political discussions across the entire platform. The search mechanism supports temporal filtering, category-based refinement, and multi-role content discovery to help users find relevant policy analyses, economic discourse, and political commentary with precision and efficiency.

pagination.description: Pagination metadata including current page, total results count, and navigation information providing users with clear indication of their position within search results

IPoliticsBbsSearchResult.description: Search result structure representing the complete response from the politicsBBS unified search endpoint. This entity encompasses both the metadata about the search operation and the actual matching content discovered through full-text search processes. The search results are optimized for efficient browsing of political and economic discussions while maintaining semantic relevance and temporal context for comprehensive content discovery across the entire politics discussion board platform.

IDateRange.description:
Date range specification for filtering search results and other temporal queries within the politicsBBS platform.

This structure enables users to narrow search results to specific time periods relevant to political and economic discussions. The date range implementation supports comprehensive search scenarios from tracking policy announcement timelines to analyzing economic trend discussions during specific legislative periods.

By establishing clear temporal boundaries, the system enables both casual educators and professional analysts to filter political and economic content with precision, ensuring relevant discourse discovery across the comprehensive timeline of democratic dialogue and fiscal policy evolution.

The structured approach helps users navigate complex political and economic discussions chronologically, making it easier to understand policy evolution, track legislative changes, and analyze the temporal progression of economic policies and political discourse on the platform. Date ranges support both recent content discovery and historical analysis for comprehensive political knowledge management.

from.description:
Start date for the specified time period, formatted as an ISO 8601 datetime string.

This field establishes the temporal starting point for date range filtering within the politicsBBS search system. The ISO 8601 format ensures consistent parsing across different systems and maintains timezone awareness, essential for a global discussion platform where political events span multiple regions.

The field is critical for enabling users to narrow search results to specific time periods relevant to their interests in political and economic discussions. Date-time boundaries support comprehensive temporal analysis for policy tracking and political discourse exploration.

to.description:
End date for the specified time period, formatted as an ISO 8601 datetime string.

This field establishes the temporal ending point for date range filtering and works in conjunction with 'from' to create a complete temporal filtering mechanism. The ISO 8601 standard ensures reliable boundary resolution for political and economic discourse content discovery.

The field enables precise limit searches to specific periods relevant to political developments or economic policy analysis. Proper date-time formatting maintains consistency across the platform for temporal query operations.

IPoliticsBbsArticleSnapshot.description: Historical snapshots of articles capturing point-in-time states for audit trails and version tracking. Snapshots preserve complete article content when articles are modified, enabling rollback capabilities and maintaining a complete history of content changes over time. This forms the content management audit trail system that allows moderators and authors to track content evolution throughout the publication lifecycle.

IPoliticsBbsContentReview.ISummary.description:
Summary information for a politics discussion board content review. This DTO contains essential details about individual content reviews with categorized reasoning, enabling moderators to quickly assess and process review requests.

Content reviews are created when articles are submitted for moderation or when they are flagged by the community. The review process focuses on ensuring content adheres to community guidelines while maintaining the platform's focus on economic and political discourse.

The summary format provides just enough information for moderation queue displays and quick decision-making, excluding detailed content data that would be visible in full detail views.

reviewed_by.description: Identifier of the moderator handling this review. Links to the responsible moderator once review begins.

updated_at.description: Timestamp of the most recent review update or change. Tracks review progression and enables timeout detection.

expires_at.description: Deadline for completing this review based on priority level. Ensures timely processing of urgent community flags.

IPoliticsBbsPopularArticles.description:
Collection of popular articles from the politics discussion board, identified through statistical analysis of view counts, recent engagement metrics, and publication recency. This response provides curated trending content discovery functionality with associated category information for proper content organization.

The popularity algorithm considers multiple factors including total view counts, recent engagement within the last 24-48 hours, and publication timeliness to surface both established discussions with sustained interest and new content gaining community attention. Only approved articles (state: approved) are included to maintain content quality standards. Articles are linked to their categories through the politics_bbs_categories table to enable category-based filtering and discovery.

This statistical response supports the atomic operation principle by delivering complete popular content data in a single API call, eliminating the need for additional filtering or sorting operations on the client side while maintaining proper category organization for the politicsBBS economic and political discussion platform.

popularArticles.description: List of popular articles sorted by popularity metrics and engagement statistics, representing current community interest on economic and political topics with category association data.
